### What does this PR do?

Add opt-in data.resume_check=off|warn|error (default off). A versioned data_manifest.json records source-byte and effective-row identities plus text preprocessing/tokenizer settings. The v1 trainer checks it before restoring actor, critic, dataloader or TransferQueue state. Identical relocated files pass; changed contents or order fail under error policy. Reusing a checkpoint directory invalidates its old sidecar before any worker write, so disabled checking or a partial overwrite cannot leave an older identity certifying new checkpoint contents. The replacement manifest is published only after dataloader and synchronous TransferQueue saving succeeds, preventing a new identity from certifying an older queue after a failed overwrite.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [focused query](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr%20is%3Aopen%20%22resume_check%22). Refreshed on 2026-10-17 against main `18cfb74852a0`.
- [x] Title follows `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

#7819 makes max_samples selection reproducible; this detects incompatible inputs and does not save/replay sampled indices. #8056 finalizes asynchronous model writes; this leaves finalization and tracker behavior unchanged. #7974 changes epoch-boundary loader restore and #8114 changes retention, neither checks input identity. No issue-closing claim is made.

### Test

Agent-run CPU validation: **65 passed**. The test command is:

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/utils/dataset/test_resume_identity_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_checkpoint_data_identity_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_checkpoint_callback_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_trainer_base_on_cpu.py
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Pre-commit: all 14 upstream hooks passed.

The original sidecar-invalidation negative control made all six overwrite regressions fail. For the review follow-up, both new split regressions and all four TransferQueue-publication regressions failed before their respective production fixes; all now pass. The tests retain the original dataset signature and config, reject unverifiable splits under error policy, and reject restoration after a failed queue overwrite before any worker/loader/queue state is loaded.

WSL Ubuntu, uv-managed Python 3.12.13, torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.12.1, Ray 2.55.1. Installed CPU/test dependencies match the current uv.lock; Megatron-Core's source dependency was omitted. This is not a complete frozen environment or official CI/GPU result. The existing CPU workflow discovers the new `*_on_cpu.py` tests; no workflow change is required.

### API, Design and Boundaries

Enable data.resume_check=error from the initial run. Old checkpoints without a sidecar are allowed by off, warned by warn, and rejected by error. Custom datasets explicitly own get_resume_signature(); a plain subclass is unverifiable. The built-in path supports local plain-text data and fast tokenizers. Ordinary dataset construction scans the source files and processed rows. Split datasets skip those discarded identity scans and remain unverifiable unless they provide their own signature. The check does not guarantee deterministic training, and a present sidecar does not prove asynchronous model shards are durable. Worker RPCs and TransferQueue transport are stubbed in trainer ordering tests; actual dataset loading and fresh-process StatefulDataLoader resume are exercised.

 Using Checkpoints to Support Fault Tolerance Training
 =====================================================
 
-Last updated: 08/24/2026.
+Last updated: 10/17/2026.
 
 There could be training errors or machine failure during the whole RLHF training process, 
 so it is recommended to enable checkpoints to minimize your loss.
@@ -38,6 +38,70 @@ Megatron:
     For FSDP, ``checkpoint.save_contents`` other than ``hf_model`` are binded together to save and
     load. We recommend to include ``model``, ``optimizer`` and ``extra`` all.
 
+Checking Data Identity Before Resume
+------------------------------------
+
+The v1 trainer (``trainer.use_v1=true``) can compare the current training
+dataset with the dataset used to save a checkpoint. Enable this from the
+initial run with ``data.resume_check=error``. The default, ``"off"``, performs
+no identity hashing or manifest checks and preserves existing behavior.
+``"warn"`` records available identity information and logs mismatches or
+unavailable information while allowing training to proceed. ``"error"``
+stops when identity is unavailable or differs, before restoring actor, critic,
+or dataloader state. This does not avoid worker initialization before resume.
+
+The built-in implementation supports local Parquet/JSON/JSONL files with
+JSON-serializable, plain-text chat rows and a fast tokenizer, without a
+processor or custom ``chat_template_func``. It hashes source bytes in file
+order, the actual rows after selection and length filtering, tokenizer state,
+chat template, tool schemas, and relevant preprocessing settings. Paths and
+modification times do not define identity: relocating identical files is
+allowed. Changing the contents without changing the row count is detected.
+Operational settings such as cache location and dataloader worker count are
+not part of dataset identity.
+
+The trainer writes ``data_manifest.json`` next to ``data.pt``. The sidecar is
+replaced atomically after saving the dataloader and, in asynchronous trainer
+modes, the TransferQueue state, before publishing the checkpoint tracker or
+calling the checkpoint callback. Preserve both files when moving a checkpoint.
+Before overwriting an existing step directory, the trainer removes its old
+sidecar, even with checking disabled. A disabled or failed save must not leave
+an older identity certifying newly written or partially replaced checkpoint files.
+With asynchronous model saves, a present sidecar is not a model-durability
+signal: model shards may still be in flight and the existing asynchronous
+checkpoint publication rules continue to apply. The check also runs before
+TransferQueue restoration in asynchronous v1 trainer modes. It does not
+change worker checkpoint finalization, retention, or remote uploads.
+The manifest stores hashes and settings, not raw rows, tokenizer vocabulary,
+or absolute input paths. This opt-in check adds a full source-file scan and
+a processed-row scan at dataset construction, including validation datasets
+constructed with the same data config; checkpoint saves reuse the signature.
+
+Old checkpoints without a sidecar are unverifiable: ``"warn"`` can continue
+with a warning, while ``"error"`` rejects them. Unsupported remote/multimodal
+datasets, slow tokenizers, and split datasets follow the same policy. Custom
+datasets must explicitly implement ``get_resume_signature()`` returning a
+nonempty, JSON-serializable dictionary whose version, content, ordering, and
+preprocessing identity they own. Subclassing ``RLHFDataset`` alone does not
+opt a custom dataset into this contract.
+
+This is a construction-time input guard, not a replay or determinism system.
+It does not restore sampled indices, repair changed data, fingerprint arbitrary
+user code, validate batch/sampler configuration, or guarantee training
+convergence or bitwise reproducibility. An unseeded selection can legitimately
+produce a different identity on restart. Do not mutate a built-in dataset or
+tokenizer after constructing it when relying on its cached signature.
+
+The CPU tests exercise actual JSON/Parquet loading, sampling/filtering,
+a fresh-process StatefulDataLoader restart, and v1 save/load ordering with
+worker RPCs stubbed:
+
+.. code-block:: bash
+
+    uv run --frozen --all-packages --extra cpu pytest -q \
+      tests/utils/dataset/test_resume_identity_on_cpu.py \
+      tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_checkpoint_data_identity_on_cpu.py

+def _trainer(tmp_path, policy="error", async_save=False):
+    trainer = _Trainer.__new__(_Trainer)
+    trainer.trainer_mode = "sync"

+                "resume_mode": "resume_path",
+                "resume_from_path": str(tmp_path / "global_step_3"),
+                "del_local_ckpt_after_load": False,
+            },
+            "actor_rollout_ref": {"actor": {"checkpoint": {"async_save": async_save}}},
+        }
+    )
+    trainer.actor_rollout_wg = MagicMock()
+    trainer.critic_wg = MagicMock()
+    trainer.checkpoint_callback = MagicMock()
+    trainer.train_dataloader = MagicMock()
+    trainer.train_dataloader.state_dict.return_value = {"step": 2}

+        assert saved["dataset"] == {"rows": "original"}
+        assert (tmp_path / "global_step_3" / "data.pt").is_file()
+
+    trainer.checkpoint_callback.on_save.side_effect = on_save
+    trainer._save_checkpoint()
+    trainer.checkpoint_callback.on_save.assert_called_once()
+    assert (tmp_path / "latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt").exists() is not async_save
+    trainer._load_checkpoint()

+def snapshot_sources(paths) -> list[dict]:

+    result = []

+        if "://" in str(source) or not path.is_file() or path.suffix not in (".parquet", ".json", ".jsonl"):

+        raise ValueError("Cannot verify resume identity after tool schema initialization failed")
+    tokenizer = dataset.tokenizer
+    tokenizer_state = {
+        "backend": json.loads(tokenizer.backend_tokenizer.to_str()),
+        "chat_template": tokenizer.chat_template,
+        "special_tokens": {
+            key: [str(token) for token in value] if isinstance(value, list) else str(value)
+            for key, value in tokenizer.special_tokens_map.items()
+        },
+        "padding_side": tokenizer.padding_side,
+        "truncation_side": tokenizer.truncation_side,

+        if not isinstance(signature, dict) or not signature:

+        manifest = {"schema_version": _VERSION, "dataset": signature}
+        return json.loads(_json_bytes(manifest))
+    except (AttributeError, NotImplementedError, TypeError, ValueError) as error:
+        message = f"Data resume identity is unavailable: {error}"
+        if policy == "error":
+            raise ValueError(message) from error
+        logger.warning(message)
+        return {"schema_version": _VERSION, "dataset": None}

+    directory = Path(checkpoint_dir)
+    if manifest is None:
+        (directory / MANIFEST_NAME).unlink(missing_ok=True)
+        return
+    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    temporary = None
+    try:
+        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="wb", dir=directory, prefix=".data_manifest-", delete=False) as stream:
+            temporary = Path(stream.name)
+            stream.write(_json_bytes(manifest))
+            stream.flush()
+            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
